Built-in function catalog (~68 functions, 10 categories)​ Category Examples String upper, lower, len, substring, trim, split, join, format, concat, pathToken Type conversion toInt, toLong, toDouble, toBoolean, toString Arithmetic add, sub, mul, div, mod, min, max, abs, round, floor, ceil Boolean not, and, or, xor, eq, ne, lt, gt, le, ge Conditional if, switch, coalesce, notEmpty, case Regex matches, replace, extract Encoding urlEncode, urlDecode, base64Encode, base64Decode, htmlEscape, htmlUnescape Date/time now, today, formatDate, parseDate Random/UUID uuid, randomInt, randomLong, randomDouble, randomString, randomChar JSON navigation jsonPath, get, keys, values, size See org.apache.juneau.commons.svl.functions for the per-class function lists with full signatures and arg style notes. Function discovery​ Three discovery channels, evaluated in order: Explicit registration — VarResolver.create().functions(MyFn.class).build(). ServiceLoader discovery — declare your implementation in META-INF/services/org.apache.juneau.commons.svl.VarFunction. VarResolver.create().defaultFunctions().build() and VarResolver.DEFAULT both load these automatically. BeanStore lookup — built-in functions are constructed through the VarResolver.Builder's BeanStore so they can themselves take constructor @Inject/@Value dependencies (rarely needed but available). Unknown function names fail lazily at resolve time (No such function 'foo') rather than at compile time, matching the existing Var registry behaviour. Hard-break removal of 11 Var classes​ The following 11 transformation Var classes are removed without @Deprecated shims: Removed Var Removed prefix Replacement IfVar $IF{...} #{if(cond, then, else)} SwitchVar $SW{...} #{switch(value, pat1:result1, ..., *:default)} (glob semantics preserved) CoalesceVar $CO{...} #{coalesce(a, b, c, ...)} NotEmptyVar $NE{...} #{notEmpty(arg)} PatternMatchVar $PM{...} #{matches(value, pattern)} PatternReplaceVar $PR{...} #{replace(value, pattern, replacement)} PatternExtractVar $PE{...} #{extract(value, pattern, groupIndex)} UpperCaseVar $UC{...} #{upper(arg)} LowerCaseVar $LC{...} #{lower(arg)} LenVar $LN{...} #{len(arg)} (single-arg) or #{len(arg, delimiter)} (two-arg parity) SubstringVar $ST{...} #{substring(arg, start)} or #{substring(arg, start, end)} VarList.addDefault() no longer registers the removed Vars; the org.apache.juneau.commons.svl.vars package no longer ships their classes. Any user code or template that still references the removed prefixes fails at resolve time with No such var '<prefix>'. The source-data Vars ($E{}, $S{}, $MF{}, $A{}, $P{} and the shortcut ${}) are unchanged. New VarTemplate compiled-template API (TODO-103)​ Added VarResolver.compile(String) → VarTemplate — tokenizes a template once and returns a reusable, threadsafe compiled form. Subsequent template.resolve(session) calls skip tokenization + var-registry lookup, walking the cached segment array directly. Added VarResolver.resolveSupplier(String) → Supplier<String> — opens a fresh session on every .get() call. Safe to share across threads. Recommended default. Added VarResolverSession.compile(String) and VarResolverSession.resolveSupplier(String) — symmetric session-bound variants. The session-bound Supplier inherits the session's threadsafety contract (i.e. not threadsafe by default). Added VarTemplate.isLiteral() — true when the template resolves to a fixed string (empty template, no variables, or all variables fold to literals via stable-value folding). Callers can fast-path purely-literal inputs. Refactored VarResolverSession.resolve(String) to delegate to compile(input).resolve(session) so there is a single tokenizer + segment-resolution path in the codebase. No behaviour change for existing callers. @Value Supplier<String> field-type autodetect​ BeanInstantiator now inspects the declared field/parameter type at injection sites carrying @Value. A Supplier<String> field receives a re-evaluating, threadsafe Supplier (delegates to VarTemplate.asSupplierWithFreshSessions(...)); a bare String field gets the one-shot resolved value as before. No @Value(supplier=true) flag is required — the field type IS the opt-in signal. Literal-only expressions (@Value("plain") Supplier<String>) take a constant-folding fast path that returns the same captured String reference on every .get() call, avoiding the per-call session allocation entirely. Worked patterns for live UUID factories, idempotency keys, jittered delays, and hot-reload config knobs are in the @Value topic page. Compile-time stable-value folding​ New default boolean Var.isStable() { return false; } SPI hook. Opt-in per Var implementation; conservative false default protects third-party Vars from accidental incorrect folding. Four built-in Vars opt in: EnvVariablesVar, SystemPropertiesVar, ManifestFileVar, ArgsVar. Compiled templates eagerly resolve these at compile time and replace the segment with a LiteralSegment — runtime dispatch is eliminated. SystemPropertiesVar's opt-in carries a documented caveat: System.setProperty(...) calls after compile do not propagate to a folded template. In practice this is the desired behaviour for the common "read once at startup" use case. ConfigVar, PropertyVar, DotenvVar, EnvFileVar stay non-stable. Their backing source can mutate at runtime (config reload, file watch, runtime Settings.set), so folding would produce stale reads. Internal perf​ BeanInstantiator's @Value resolution path caches a VarTemplate per distinct expression in ValueResolver.TEMPLATE_CACHE. Repeated bean construction reads the cached form rather than re-tokenizing. RestOpContext.pathMatchers Memoizer now goes through vr.compile(p).resolve(session) explicitly so the framework hot loop exercises the compiled-template seam. If we ever switch to per-request dynamic path resolution, only the .resolve(session) step moves to the request handler — the compile is already done at context-build time. Micro-benchmark (juneau-utest/.../VarResolver_Benchmark_Test): compile-once + resolve-N is ~1.7× faster than compile-per-call for plain ${...} templates and ~1.4× for #{...} script templates on a representative machine. The headline ≥ 2× / ≥ 5× targets from the plan apply to comparisons against the pre-9.5 legacy ad-hoc dispatcher, which is no longer in the tree — the unified compiled-form path is now the baseline. Migration​ For any SVL template that uses one of the 11 removed Var prefixes, rewrite to #{...}. Cookbook: Before After $UC{$S{user.name}} #{upper(${user.name})} $IF{$S{prod},prod.key,dev.key} #{if(${prod}, prod.key, dev.key)} $SW{$S{os},*win*:Windows,*:Unix} #{switch(${os}, *win*:Windows, *:Unix)} $PR{$S{name},[aeiou],*} #{replace(${name}, [aeiou], *)} $LN{a,b,c,,} #{len(a,b,c, ,)} $ST{hello,2,4} #{substring(hello, 2, 4)} The full ${...} shortcut, $S{}/$E{}/$MF{}/$A{}/$P{} source vars, and $C{} config var keep their existing syntax — no migration required for those.
documents.s: SVL overhaul: #{...} scripting + VarTemplate compilation (TODO-102 + TODO-103)

documents.t: org.apache.juneau.commons.lang.Value renamed to Holder. The mutable reference-wrapper utility class has been renamed to Holder<T> to resolve an import-name collision with the @Value injection annotation. Update import statements: import org.apache.juneau.commons.lang.Value → import org.apache.juneau.commons.lang.Holder. No behavioral change. XValue primitive-holder companions renamed to XHolder. The nine typed primitive-holder subclasses have been renamed for consistency with the Value → Holder rename: BooleanValue → BooleanHolder, ByteValue → ByteHolder, CharValue → CharHolder, DoubleValue → DoubleHolder, FloatValue → FloatHolder, IntegerValue → IntegerHolder, LongValue → LongHolder, ShortValue → ShortHolder, StringValue → StringHolder. Update import statements and type references accordingly. No behavioral change.

LocalDir.resolve(...) now enforces path-traversal boundary defensively (consistent with FileUtils.resolveSafely(...)). On the filesystem-root branch, resolution is delegated to FileUtils.resolveSafely(...) which rejects any path that escapes the configured root (via ../, absolute-path injection, or symlinks pointing outside the root) with IllegalArgumentException. On the classpath-resource branch, paths containing .. segments are likewise rejected. This makes LocalDir the single-source-of-truth CWE-22 enforcement point — callers no longer need to pre-validate paths before calling resolve(...).

Added org.apache.juneau.config.ConfigPropertySourceProvider, a META-INF/services-discovered PropertySourceProvider that bridges Config.getSystemDefault() (i.e. the classpath juneau.cfg / default.cfg / application.cfg / etc. discovered by Config.getCandidateSystemDefaultConfigNames()) into the process-wide Settings singleton. Resolution is lazy — Config.getSystemDefault() is invoked on the first Settings.get(name) lookup rather than at SPI registration time. This avoids a static-initialization cycle (Settings.<clinit> → useServiceLoader() → ConfigPropertySourceProvider.create() → Config.<clinit> → Cache.create() → Utils.env(...) → Settings.<clinit>) and a runtime reentrance cycle (Config.findSystemDefault() looking up "juneau.configFile" through every registered source, including this one). A thread-local guard short-circuits the reentrant lookup; any throwable while Config is mid-initialisation is treated as "not yet available" without memoising the failure. The provider is silent when no classpath Config exists — every lookup returns missing(), no log noise, no exception. The provider's order() is 100, deliberately low — so any programmatic Settings.get().addSource(...) registered later (microservice, RestContext, Spring) shadows the classpath default at lookup time.

Added optional YAML config support to juneau-config alongside the existing INI/CFG format. Added format selection via config name extension (.yml / .yaml) and explicit builder methods (.yaml() / .ini()). Added path-style section support (e.g. [foo/bar/baz]) to align INI sections with nested YAML mappings. Updated default FileStore extension search order to include cfg,yml,yaml (with cfg remaining first for backward compatibility).

Added a new property-source SPI naming model: PropertySource / PropertyStore and functional variants. Added PropertySourceProvider (ServiceLoader SPI) so ambient sources can be auto-registered onto Settings. Added built-in property sources for args, manifest entries, system properties, environment variables, and .env. Added runtime source wiring via Settings.addSource(PropertySource) to allow explicit opt-in sources. Added PropertyVar ($P{key[,default]}) as the SVL unified property-stack resolver. Existing $S / $E / $A / $MF vars remain supported as source-specific resolvers, now aligned with the unified settings model. Breaking: SettingSource, SettingStore, FunctionalSource, and FunctionalStore have been removed outright (no deprecation shims). Migrate to PropertySource, PropertyStore, FunctionalPropertySource, and FunctionalPropertyStore respectively.

A comprehensive rename of annotation and engine types to clarify the distinction between Java-bean-structure types (which keep BeanXxx names) and marshalling-process types (which are now MarshallingXxx). Annotation Renames (breaking)​ Old New @Bean (marshall) @Marshalled @BeanApply @MarshalledApply @Beanp @MarshalledProp @BeanpApply @MarshalledPropApply @Beanc @MarshalledCtor @BeancApply @MarshalledCtorApply @BeanIgnore @MarshalledIgnore @BeanIgnoreApply @MarshalledIgnoreApply @BeanConfig @MarshalledConfig Engine Type Renames (breaking)​ Old New BeanContext MarshallingContext BeanContextable MarshallingContextable BeanSession MarshallingSession BeanTraverseContext MarshallingTraverseContext BeanTraverseSession MarshallingTraverseSession BeanRecursionException MarshallingRecursionException BeanStringSwap MarshallingStringSwap BeanContextConverter MarshallingContextConverter BeanDefMapper MarshallingDefMapper BeanContext.DEFAULT MarshallingContext.DEFAULT Unchanged Types (clarification)​ The following BeanXxx types model the Java bean structure and are deliberately unchanged: BeanMap, BeanMeta, BeanPropertyMeta, BeanPropertyValue, BeanPropertyConsumer, BeanRegistry, BeanDictionaryMap, BeanDictionaryList, BeanProxyInvocationHandler, BeanDiff. Package Moves (Phase 5a of bean-layer split)​ As part of the bean-layer split (separating bean-modeling from marshalling), the BeanInterceptor type was moved into the new org.apache.juneau.commons.bean package in juneau-commons: Old New org.apache.juneau.swap.MarshallingInterceptor org.apache.juneau.commons.bean.BeanInterceptor This is both a rename (back to the pre-9.5 BeanInterceptor name) and a package move. Source code referencing the type by simple name through wildcard imports may need to update its import from org.apache.juneau.swap.* to org.apache.juneau.commons.bean.* (or add an explicit import). New Type: BeanConfigContext (Phase 5b of bean-layer split)​ A new org.apache.juneau.commons.bean.BeanConfigContext POJO carries the runtime bean-modeling settings — visibility thresholds, the beans*Require* toggles, fluent-setter detection, property naming, the bean-type property name, the not-a-bean exclusion sets, the active BeanStore, the active AnnotationProvider, and an optional Predicate<ClassInfo> override for isNotABean. It is the runtime sibling of the @BeanConfig annotation introduced in Phase 3. MarshallingContext now exposes getBeanConfigContext() returning a memoized snapshot view, so consumers that only need bean-modeling settings can depend on commons.bean without referencing any marshalling-aware types. This is foundational infrastructure for the relocation of BeanMap / BeanMeta / BeanPropertyMeta and friends into commons.bean (completed in Phase 5c below). Bean-Runtime Cluster Moved to commons.bean (Phase 5c of bean-layer split)​ The seven core bean-runtime types have been physically moved out of org.apache.juneau (in juneau-marshall) into org.apache.juneau.commons.bean (in juneau-commons): Old New org.apache.juneau.BeanMap org.apache.juneau.commons.bean.BeanMap org.apache.juneau.BeanMapEntry org.apache.juneau.commons.bean.BeanMapEntry org.apache.juneau.BeanMeta org.apache.juneau.commons.bean.BeanMeta org.apache.juneau.BeanPropertyMeta (and its Builder inner class) org.apache.juneau.commons.bean.BeanPropertyMeta org.apache.juneau.BeanPropertyValue org.apache.juneau.commons.bean.BeanPropertyValue org.apache.juneau.BeanPropertyConsumer org.apache.juneau.commons.bean.BeanPropertyConsumer org.apache.juneau.BeanProxyInvocationHandler org.apache.juneau.commons.bean.BeanProxyInvocationHandler The @Name annotation also moved as part of this work: Old New org.apache.juneau.annotation.Name org.apache.juneau.commons.bean.Name After these moves, juneau-commons compiles standalone with no dependency on juneau-marshall, and the bean-modeling layer in commons.bean is fully self-contained. Source code referencing any of these types by simple name through wildcard imports must update from org.apache.juneau.* (or org.apache.juneau.annotation.*) to org.apache.juneau.commons.bean.*. Fully-qualified @org.apache.juneau.annotation.Name(...) references must be rewritten to @org.apache.juneau.commons.bean.Name(...). Bean-Modeling Annotation Surface (Phase 5c)​ The bean-modeling attributes have been split out of the marshalling-side @Marshalled family into a parallel set of commons-side annotations. The marshalling-side annotations retain only the marshalling-only attributes; both annotations are still consulted on the marshalling-side path so a class can carry both without conflict. Commons-side (new) Marshalling-side sibling Carries @BeanType @Marshalled Class-level bean-modeling attributes: properties / p, excludeProperties / xp, readOnlyProperties / ro, writeOnlyProperties / wo, unsorted, findFluentSetters, propertyNamer, interfaceClass, stopClass, factory. @BeanProp @MarshalledProp Property-level bean-modeling attributes: name / value, ro, wo, type, params, elementType, factory. @BeanCtor @MarshalledCtor Constructor mapping: properties. @BeanIgnore @MarshalledIgnore Bean-property / class ignore (with ignoreAccessors for fields). @BeanConfig @MarshalledConfig Class- / method-level bean-modeling config (visibility thresholds, beans*Require* toggles, fluent setters, property naming, not-a-bean exclusions, etc.). @Marshalled retains the marshalling-only attributes: as, description, dictionary, example, implClass, interceptor, typeName, typePropertyName. @MarshalledProp retains its marshalling-only attributes (e.g. dictionary, format). Contributions from the bean-modeling and marshalling-side annotations are merged when building the bean filter on the marshalling-side path. commons.bean SPI Surface (Phase 5c)​ To plug the relocated bean-runtime types back into the marshalling layer, several new SPI types have been added to org.apache.juneau.commons.bean: SPI Type Description Marshalling-side implementation BeanInfo<T> Bean-modeling type-info seam. Extends ClassInfoTyped<T>; exposes isBean(), isUri(), getElementType(), getKeyType(), getValueType(), canCreateNewInstance(...), getOptionalDefault(), getBeanConfigContext(), getMarshallingContext(). ClassMeta<T> extends this. BeanSession Bean-modeling session SPI (convertToType, convertToMemberType, toBeanMap, parseToMap(CharSequence), parseToList(CharSequence)). MarshallingSession implements this. BeanFilter Per-class filter surface (properties / excludeProperties / readOnlyProperties / writeOnlyProperties / typeName / interfaceClass / stopClass / propertyNamer / beanDictionary / interceptor hooks). MarshalledFilter implements this. BeanRegistryLookup Bean-dictionary lookup surface. BeanRegistry implements this. BeanMetaInitializer Marshalling-side BeanMeta construction hooks (filter discovery, type-name resolution, bean-registry assembly, parent-chain type-name lookup). NOOP default for the commons-side path. MarshalledBeanMetaInitializer implements this. BeanPropertyPostProcessor Marshalling-side BeanPropertyMeta.Builder post-processing (@MarshalledProp / @Swap / @Uri reads, swap-aware read/write transforms). NOOP default for the commons-side path. MarshalledPropertyPostProcessor implements this. BeanTypeResolver Marshalling-side type-resolution SPI used by BeanPropertyMeta.Builder.validate(...). MarshallingContext implements this. BeanConfigContext carries all of these so the bean-modeling layer can drive bean-meta construction with or without a marshalling context. Type and Method Renames (Phase 5c, breaking)​ The bean-modeling SPI seam was renamed and several accessors aligned with the new SPI surface: Old New Notes BeanTypeInfo<T> (commons.bean) BeanInfo<T> Full type rename. No deprecation shim. Delegate#getClassMeta() Delegate#getBeanInfo() Returns BeanInfo<T>. BeanMap#getClassMeta() BeanMap#getBeanInfo() Returns BeanInfo<T>. BeanMeta#getClassMeta() BeanMeta#getBeanInfo() Returns BeanInfo<T>. BeanPropertyMeta#getClassMeta() BeanPropertyMeta#getBeanInfo() Returns BeanInfo<?>. BeanPropertyValue#getClassMeta() BeanPropertyValue#getBeanInfo() Returns BeanInfo<?>. BeanMap#setMarshallingSession(BeanSession) BeanMap#setBeanSession(BeanSession) No deprecated shim. Existing call sites that pass a MarshallingSession (which implements BeanSession) continue to compile after the rename. MarshallingContext.getClassMeta(Class) and MarshallingContext.getClassMeta(Type, Type...) are intentionally unchanged — they still resolve ClassMeta directly on the marshalling side. The BeanPropertyPostProcessor SPI also tightened its signature now that BeanPropertyMeta.Builder lives in commons.bean: // Before void process(Object marshallingContext, Object builder); // After void process(Object marshallingContext, BeanPropertyMeta.Builder builder); Removed APIs (Phase 5c)​ BeanFilter.getMarshalledClass() — Dead/unused accessor on the bean-filter SPI. Removed along with the backing marshalledClass field on MarshalledFilter and the MarshalledFilter.Builder(Class<?>) / MarshalledFilter.create(Class<T>) overloads. Use BeanFilter.getBeanClass() (returns ClassInfoTyped<?>) instead. ClassInfo Additions (Phase 5c)​ Two pure class-check helpers were lifted up to org.apache.juneau.commons.reflect.ClassInfo alongside the existing isArray(), isMap(), isBoolean(), and isVoid() siblings: ClassInfo#isObject() — Returns true when this class is exactly java.lang.Object. ClassInfo#isOptional() — Returns true when this class is java.util.Optional. API Visibility Widening (Phase 5c)​ Several previously protected or package-private members were widened so marshalling-side callers (and juneau-marshall-rdf extensions) can still reach them across the new package boundary: BeanMeta.BeanMetaValue record made public (and its optBeanMeta() accessor). BeanMeta accessors getConstructor(), getConstructorArgs(), hasConstructor(), newBean(Object) widened protected → public. BeanMap constructor (T, BeanMeta<T>) and setBeanSession(BeanSession) widened protected → public. BeanPropertyMeta.Builder fields innerField, getter, setter, rawTypeMeta, swap, readTransform, writeTransform, dictionaryClasses, isUri, and typeMeta widened package-private → public (consumed by MarshalledPropertyPostProcessor). BeanPropertyValue.properties() widened protected → public. New Feature: @Marshalled(as=STRING) Strategy​ A new MarshalledAs enum with values DETECT (default) and STRING has been added to @Marshalled: // Force a type to serialize as its toString() value, bypassing bean detection. @Marshalled(as=STRING) public class MyType { @Override public String toString() { return "my-string-form"; } } @Marshalled(as=STRING) replaces two earlier patterns: The BeanStringSwap class (now MarshallingStringSwap; kept for custom format overrides) The @BeanIgnore-on-class-then-toString() pattern Updated @MarshalledIgnore TYPE Semantics (breaking)​ Applying @MarshalledIgnore to a class now skips serialization entirely (outputs null) instead of falling through to toString(): // Before (@BeanIgnore on class → toString()) @BeanIgnore public class OldClass { @Override public String toString() { return "value"; } } // Serialized as: "value" // After (@MarshalledIgnore on class → null) @MarshalledIgnore public class NewClass { ... } // Serialized as: null // Migration: if you need toString() behavior, use @Marshalled(as=STRING) instead @Marshalled(as=STRING) public class NewClass { @Override public String toString() { return "value"; } } // Serialized as: "value" Migration: If you previously used @BeanIgnore on a class to force toString() serialization, replace it with @Marshalled(as=STRING). If you truly want to suppress serialization (output null), use @MarshalledIgnore.

The @MarshalledProp(properties=...) attribute has been removed. The attribute was used to limit which child properties of a nested bean/map are rendered by serializers: // Before — only "f1" was rendered on each child. public class MyClass { @MarshalledProp(properties="f1") public MyChildClass x1 = new MyChildClass(); } // After — the attribute no longer exists; nested beans render in full. public class MyClass { public MyChildClass x1 = new MyChildClass(); } The related internal types are gone too: BeanPropertyMeta.applyChildPropertiesFilter(...), BeanPropertyMeta.getProperties() (override-list accessor), and the underlying properties field/builder setter. BeanMetaFiltered (sole purpose was wrapping a BeanMeta with a filtered property list). Migration: If you need per-property filtering for a serialization, use a custom BeanFilter/@Marshalled(properties=...) at the bean-class level instead, or configure include/exclude lists on the MarshallingContext.Builder. The marshalling-context-level filtering pre-dated @MarshalledProp(properties) and remains fully supported.

On a field whose type is not a Map, @Beanp("*") (or @Beanp(name="*")) no longer tries to register a dyna property. The property name is taken from the field (via the configured PropertyNamer); other @Beanp attributes still apply. Map fields keep the dyna property * as before.

BasicHtmlDocTemplate now treats bare navlink lines like request:?Accept=... or request:/?Accept=... (no label: prefix) as full marshall URIs. Previously the first : split dropped the scheme, producing relative href values that browsers resolved under the current path (e.g. .../request:?Accept=...). The same rejoin applies to servlet: and context: when the part after the colon starts with /, ?, or #. Labeled navlinks (e.g. JSON: request:?Accept=...) were already correct; the bug affected bare entries where the text before the first : is only the marshall scheme name.
documents.s: HTML documentation: bare request: / servlet: / context: navlinks

documents.t: Juneau now includes built-in TOML (Tom's Obvious Minimal Language) v1.0.0 serialization and parsing support, implemented entirely without external library dependencies. TOML is a configuration file format widely used in projects like Cargo (Rust) and Python's pyproject.toml. New Classes​ TomlSerializer - Serializes POJOs to TOML format with tables, key-value pairs, and proper escaping. TomlParser - Parses TOML input into POJOs using a tokenizer-based parser. Toml - Convenience marshaller pairing TomlSerializer and TomlParser. BasicTomlConfig - REST configuration interface for TOML-only resources. Features​ The implementation conforms to the TOML v1.0.0 specification: // Serialize a map to TOML Map<String, Object> config = Map.of("name", "myapp", "port", 8080); String toml = Toml.of(config); // Produces: name = "myapp" // port = 8080 // Parse TOML into JsonMap or beans JsonMap parsed = Toml.to(toml, JsonMap.class); MyConfig config = Toml.to(toml, MyConfig.class); Tables - [section] and nested [parent.child] tables Inline tables - {key = "value"} for simple nested structures Arrays - Homogeneous arrays of primitives, strings, and inline tables Strings - Basic, literal, and multi-line variants Dates and times - ISO 8601 (LocalDate, LocalDateTime, OffsetDateTime, etc.) Media Types​ Produces: application/toml Accepts: application/toml, text/toml TOML is included in BasicUniversalConfig by default, or can be used standalone via BasicTomlConfig. See TOML Basics for full documentation.

Juneau now includes built-in JSONL (JSON Lines / NDJSON) serialization and parsing support. JSONL is a text format where each line is a valid JSON value, widely used for LLM fine-tuning datasets, streaming AI inference, log aggregation, and bulk data pipelines. New Classes​ JsonlSerializer - Serializes POJOs to JSONL format with one JSON value per line. JsonlParser - Parses JSONL input into POJOs, reading one line at a time. Jsonl - Convenience marshaller pairing JsonlSerializer and JsonlParser. BasicJsonlConfig - REST configuration interface for JSONL-only resources. Features​ Each line is a compact JSON value; collections and arrays serialize one element per line. Full round-trip parity with JSON for beans, maps, collections, scalars, and ObjectSwaps. Supports streaming (Iterator, Iterable, Stream) for lazy serialization. Date/time and Duration types serialized as ISO 8601 strings. // Serialize a list of beans to JSONL List<Person> people = List.of(new Person("Alice", 30), new Person("Bob", 25)); String jsonl = Jsonl.of(people); // Produces: // {"name":"Alice","age":30} // {"name":"Bob","age":25} // Parse JSONL into a list of beans List<Person> parsed = Jsonl.to(jsonl, List.class, Person.class); Media Types​ Produces: application/jsonl Accepts: application/jsonl, application/x-ndjson, text/jsonl JSONL is included in BasicUniversalConfig by default, or can be used standalone via BasicJsonlConfig. See JSONL Basics for full documentation.

Juneau now ships with a native serializer / parser for the WHATWG Server-Sent Events wire format (text/event-stream). SSE is the standard one-way push channel used by browsers (EventSource) and most LLM streaming APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) for progress events, partial responses, and long-lived telemetry feeds. New Classes (in org.apache.juneau.sse)​ SseEvent — bean carrying the four spec fields (event, data, id, retry). The data payload is a pre-serialized string — callers serialize their typed payload through their marshaller of choice (e.g. Json.of(...)) and assign the resulting string. SseSerializer extends WriterSerializer — produces text/event-stream. Accepts a single SseEvent, an Iterable, a Stream, or an SseEvent[] array. Calls Writer.flush() after every event so events are pushed to the client immediately (essential for server-push and AI streaming). SseParser extends ReaderParser — eager parse of a closed text/event-stream into List<SseEvent>, SseEvent[], or a single SseEvent. SseEventReader — public Iterator<SseEvent> + Closeable for line-driven streaming over a caller-owned Reader. The intended API for long-lived SSE streams that outlive the standard parser-session lifecycle. Sse marshaller (in org.apache.juneau.marshaller) — convenience pairing of SseSerializer and SseParser with of(...) / to(...) shortcuts. Features​ Full WHATWG parse-algorithm compliance: all three line terminators (CR, LF, CR LF), one-time UTF-8 BOM strip, field:value field splitting with optional-space stripping after the colon, multi-line data: concatenation, comment-line (: heartbeat) skipping, and the spec-defined ignore rules for id containing U+0000 and non-digit retry values. Per-event Writer.flush() inside SseSerializerSession.doSerialize(...) so SSE actually works as a push channel (without it, events would buffer and only land at end-of-response). SseSerializer.writeComment(Writer, String) helper for emitting SSE heartbeat / keep-alive comment lines on long-lived connections. Example​ // Serialize a list of events to SSE wire format List<SseEvent> events = List.of( new SseEvent("progress", "step 1").setId("1"), new SseEvent("progress", "step 2").setId("2") ); String wire = Sse.of(events); // Produces: // event: progress // data: step 1 // id: 1 // // event: progress // data: step 2 // id: 2 // // Parse SSE wire format back into a list of events List<SseEvent> parsed = Sse.to(wire, List.class, SseEvent.class); REST integration​ SSE is not added to BasicUniversalConfig (it's a streaming, one-way push format with different semantics from the regular content-negotiation marshallers). Register it explicitly per-endpoint: @Rest(serializers = SseSerializer.class) public class MyStreamResource { @RestGet("/events") public List<SseEvent> stream() { return List.of( new SseEvent("progress", "step 1"), new SseEvent("progress", "step 2") ); } } Media Types​ Produces / accepts: text/event-stream See SSE Basics for full documentation.

Juneau now includes built-in BSON (Binary JSON) serialization and parsing support, implemented without external library dependencies. BSON is the binary serialization format used by MongoDB, extending JSON with typed integers (int32/int64), native datetime, decimal128, and binary data. New Classes​ BsonSerializer - Serializes POJOs to BSON format (little-endian, length-prefixed documents). BsonParser - Parses BSON input into POJOs. Bson - Convenience marshaller pairing BsonSerializer and BsonParser. BasicBsonConfig - REST configuration interface for BSON-only resources. Features​ Full Java type mapping: beans/maps → documents, collections/arrays → BSON arrays, byte[] → binary (0x05), dates → datetime (0x09) or ISO 8601 string, BigDecimal/BigInteger → decimal128 (0x13). REST integration: RestClient.bson(), RestRequest.bson(), MockRestClient.bson(), MockRestRequest.bson(). Annotations: @Bson, @BsonConfig (addBeanTypes, writeDatesAsDatetime). Round-trip parity with JSON for all standard data types; included in RoundTripTest_Base. // Serialize a bean to BSON Person p = new Person("Alice", 30); byte[] bson = Bson.of(p); // Parse BSON into a bean Person parsed = Bson.to(bson, Person.class); // REST client with BSON RestClient client = RestClient.create().uri("http://localhost:8080").bson().build(); byte[] response = client.get("/api/person/1").bson().run().body(); Media Types​ Produces: application/bson Accepts: application/bson BSON is included in BasicUniversalConfig by default, or can be used standalone via BasicBsonConfig. See BSON Basics for full documentation.

Juneau now includes built-in CBOR per RFC 8949 serialization and parsing support, implemented without external library dependencies. CBOR is a compact binary format designed for extremely small code size and message size, widely used in IoT, constrained environments, COSE (CBOR Object Signing and Encryption), and WebAuthn. New Classes​ CborSerializer - Serializes POJOs to CBOR format (RFC 8949, compact integer encoding, definite-length arrays/maps). CborParser - Parses CBOR input into POJOs. Cbor - Convenience marshaller pairing CborSerializer and CborParser. BasicCborConfig - REST configuration interface for CBOR-only resources. Features​ Full Java type mapping: beans/maps → CBOR maps (major type 5), collections/arrays → CBOR arrays (major type 4), strings → text strings (major type 3), integers → compact encoding (major types 0/1), floats → IEEE 754 (0xFA/0xFB), byte[] → byte strings (major type 2). SpacedHex and Base64 variants for text-friendly output (debugging, testing). REST integration: CBOR included in BasicUniversalConfig and RestClient.universal(). Annotations: @Cbor, @CborConfig (addBeanTypesCbor, useTags). Round-trip parity with JSON for standard data types. // Serialize a bean to CBOR Person p = new Person("Alice", 30); byte[] cbor = Cbor.of(p); // Parse CBOR into a bean Person parsed = Cbor.to(cbor, Person.class); Media Types​ Produces: application/cbor Accepts: application/cbor CBOR is included in BasicUniversalConfig by default, or can be used standalone via BasicCborConfig. See CBOR Basics for full documentation.

The HoconParser now supports additional HOCON features for configuration files: += array append - list += item appends to an existing array or creates [item] if the key does not exist Self-referential substitution - path = ${path}"/bin" appends to the previous value (e.g. /usr → /usr/bin) Value concatenation - Adjacent values concatenate: path = /usr "/local" → "/usr/local" Array concatenation - [1, 2] [3, 4] → [1, 2, 3, 4] Object concatenation - {a: 1} {b: 2} → {a: 1, b: 2} See HOCON Basics for full documentation.

Juneau now includes built-in JCS (JSON Canonicalization Scheme) per RFC 8785. JCS produces a deterministic, byte-for-byte canonical representation of JSON data, enabling reliable cryptographic operations such as hashing and digital signing. New Classes​ JcsSerializer - Serializes POJOs to canonical JSON with sorted properties, ECMAScript number formatting, and no whitespace. Jcs - Convenience marshaller pairing JcsSerializer and JsonParser (JCS output is valid JSON). Features​ Deterministic output - Same input always produces identical output for hashing/signing. No whitespace - Compact single-line output. Sorted properties - UTF-16 code unit order, applied recursively to nested objects. ECMAScript number serialization - Shortest round-trip representation per ECMA-262. Full round-trip - Use JsonParser to parse JCS output. // Serialize to canonical JSON Person alice = new Person("Alice", 30); String canonical = Jcs.of(alice); // Produces: {"age":30,"name":"Alice"} // Parse canonical JSON (same as regular JSON) Person parsed = Jcs.to(canonical, Person.class); Limitations​ NaN and Infinity - Rejected; throws SerializeException. Lone surrogates - Strings with unpaired UTF-16 surrogates throw SerializeException. Media type - Output is application/json; JCS does not define a separate media type. JCS is included in BasicUniversalConfig by default. See JCS Basics for full documentation.

JsonSerializer and JsonParser now strictly enforce RFC 8259 JSON (double-quoted strings only). Single-quoted JSON, comments, trailing commas, and unquoted keys are rejected by JsonParser. For JSON5 syntax (single quotes, comments, trailing commas, unquoted keys), use Json5Serializer and Json5Parser instead. Changes​ JsonParser - Strict RFC 8259 only; single-quoted strings throw ParseException. Use Json5Parser for JSON5 input. JsonSerializer - Produces strict JSON by default. Use Json5Serializer for JSON5-style output (single quotes, etc.). Removed - JsonSerializer.json5() and JsonParser.Strict; use Json5Serializer and Json5Parser directly. BeanContext.beanToStringSerializer - Now uses Json5Serializer for toString() output (more human-readable). ComboRoundTripTest - Framework now distinguishes json vs json5; use json()/json5() builder methods on ComboRoundTrip_Tester accordingly. juneau-examples-rest-jetty-ftest - SamplesMicroservice and RootResourcesTest now use Json5Parser to match server output (RootResources uses quoteChar="'" for testing). See JSON Basics, JSON Parsers, and JSON 5 for full documentation.

Bean properties are now serialized in alphabetical order by default across all serializers. Previously, the default was natural JVM order and opting in to sorted output required explicit configuration. New API: @Bean(unsorted=true) — Opts a specific bean class out of the default sorted order, using natural JVM property order instead. BeanContext.Builder.unsortedProperties() — Disables sorted properties globally for all beans. BeanContext.Builder.unsortedProperties(Class<?>...on) — Disables sorted properties for specific bean classes only. BeanFilter.Builder.unsortedProperties() — Per-bean-filter opt-out of sorted properties. BeanFilter.isUnsortedProperties() — Returns true if this bean filter opts out of sorting. BeanSession.isUnsortedProperties() — Session-level accessor for the unsorted flag. Migration: // Before: opt in to sorted output @Bean(sort=true) public class MyBean { ... } // After: sorted is the default, opt out with unsorted=true @Bean(unsorted=true) public class MyBean { ... } // opts out of default sorted behavior // Before: global sorted flag required explicit opt-in JsonSerializer s = JsonSerializer.create().sortProperties().build(); // After: sorted by default; use unsortedProperties() to opt out JsonSerializer s = JsonSerializer.create().unsortedProperties().build(); Removed API: @Bean(sort) — Removed. Use @Bean(unsorted=true) with inverted semantics. BeanContext.Builder.sortProperties() / sortProperties(boolean) — Removed. Use unsortedProperties(). BeanContext.Builder.sortProperties(Class<?>...on) — Removed. Use unsortedProperties(Class<?>...on). BeanContextable.Builder.sortProperties() / sortProperties(Class<?>...on) — Removed. Use unsortedProperties() / unsortedProperties(Class<?>...on). BeanFilter.Builder.sortProperties() / sortProperties(boolean) — Removed. Use unsortedProperties(). BeanFilter.isSortProperties() / BeanSession.isSortProperties() — Removed. Use isUnsortedProperties(). BeanMeta.isSortProperties() — Removed. Use isUnsortedProperties(). All serializer/parser builder sortProperties() / sortProperties(Class<?>...on) overrides — Removed. Internal rename: BeanMeta.sortProperties field — Renamed to unsortedProperties with inverted semantics. The field now stores true when the bean opts out of default sorted order, rather than true when sorted is explicitly enabled.
documents.s: Sorted Bean Properties by Default; @Bean(unsorted) Opt-Out

documents.t: @BeanIgnore gains ignoreAccessors (default false) for use on fields. When ignoreAccessors = true, BeanMeta also excludes the matching JavaBean accessor pair (getX/setX, or isX for booleans) from bean property discovery, so the property is omitted from serialization, parsing, and BeanMap metadata while accessors can remain for other frameworks. The default false preserves existing behavior: @BeanIgnore on a field only excludes the field from field-based discovery; accessors can still expose the property (for example when beanFieldVisibility is NONE and only methods are considered). Applies to Juneau’s default introspection and to BeanContext.Builder.useJavaBeanIntrospector() (BeanInfo / PropertyDescriptor discovery). Property names follow the same rules as field discovery: @Beanp / @Name on the field, if present, otherwise the configured PropertyNamer on the field name. See @BeanIgnore Annotation.

Juneau now includes built-in Protobuf Text Format serialization and parsing support, implemented without external library dependencies. This is the human-readable text format (not the binary wire format), suitable for configuration, debugging, and interop with tools that use the text format. New Classes​ ProtoSerializer - Serializes POJOs to Protobuf Text Format. ProtoParser - Parses Protobuf Text Format into POJOs. Proto - Convenience marshaller pairing ProtoSerializer and ProtoParser. BasicProtoConfig - REST configuration interface for Proto-only resources. Features​ No .proto schema files required—Java bean metadata provides type information. Supports beans, maps, collections, scalars, repeated fields, and nested messages. Date/time and Duration types serialized as ISO 8601 strings. Annotations: @Proto (comment), @ProtoConfig (useListSyntaxForBeans, useColonForMessages). // Serialize a bean to Protobuf Text Format Person p = new Person("Alice", 30); String proto = Proto.of(p); // Produces: name: "Alice" // age: 30 // Parse Protobuf Text Format into a bean Person parsed = Proto.to(proto, Person.class); Media Types​ Produces: text/protobuf Accepts: text/protobuf, text/x-protobuf Proto is included in BasicUniversalConfig by default, or can be used standalone via BasicProtoConfig. See Protobuf Basics for full documentation.

The CsvParser is now fully implemented. Previously, parsing always threw "Not implemented.". The parser supports the same range of target types as other Juneau parsers. New Class​ CsvReader - Low-level RFC 4180-compliant CSV reader used internally by CsvParserSession. Features​ The parser reads a header row to discover column names, then maps each subsequent data row to the target type: String csv = "name,age
Alice,30
Bob,25
"; // Parse into a list of beans List<Person> people = CsvParser.DEFAULT.parse(csv, List.class, Person.class); // Parse into a list of maps List<Map<String,String>> rows = CsvParser.DEFAULT.parse(csv, List.class, Map.class); // Parse a single bean Person p = CsvParser.DEFAULT.parse("name,age
Alice,30
", Person.class); Supported target types: Target Type Behavior Collection<Bean> / Bean[] Header row → property names; each data row → one bean. Collection<Map> / Map[] Header row → map keys; each data row → one map. Collection<SimpleType> / SimpleType[] value column → each row coerced to element type. Single Bean Header row + one data row → one bean. Single Map Header row + one data row → one map. Object Returns a JsonList of JsonMap entries. Type coercion converts string cell values to the target property type, including primitives, enums, date/time types, and any type supported by Juneau's convertToType(). The unquoted literal null in a cell is parsed as Java null.

RFC 4180 Quote Escaping: CsvWriter.writeEntry() now correctly escapes embedded double-quote characters by doubling them (" → ""), as required by RFC 4180. Previously, values containing embedded quotes were written with unescaped quotes, producing invalid CSV. DynaBean Support: The CsvSerializer now serializes DynaBeans (dynamic beans not directly identified as beans by ClassMeta.isBean()) by attempting toBeanMap() on each entry. Round-Trip Tests: CsvSerializer and CsvParser are now included in the RoundTripTest_Base framework (as tester #18), skipping inputs that are not flat collections. See CSV Basics for full documentation.

Juneau now includes built-in Markdown serialization and parsing support, implemented entirely without external library dependencies. Markdown output is optimized for both human readability and LLM/AI consumption, with fragment mode (tables, lists) and document mode (headings + tables) for nested structures. New Classes​ MarkdownSerializer - Serializes POJOs to Markdown fragment output (tables, bulleted lists). MarkdownDocSerializer - Extends MarkdownSerializer for full documents with heading-based structure. MarkdownParser - Parses Markdown tables and bulleted lists back into POJOs. MarkdownDocParser - Parses Markdown documents with headings into nested bean structure. Markdown - Convenience marshaller pairing MarkdownSerializer and MarkdownParser. MarkdownDoc - Convenience marshaller pairing MarkdownDocSerializer and MarkdownDocParser. Features​ Fragment mode: Beans and maps as key-value tables; uniform collections as multi-column tables; simple collections as bulleted lists. Document mode: Nested beans under sub-headings (H2, H3, etc.); customizable title, header, and footer content. Inline complex values: Nested beans and collections in table cells rendered as backtick-wrapped JSON5. Media Types​ Produces: text/markdown Accepts: text/markdown, text/x-markdown Markdown is included in BasicUniversalConfig and RestClient.universal() by default. See Markdown Basics for full documentation.

Juneau now includes built-in YAML serialization and parsing support, implemented entirely without external library dependencies. Like all other Juneau serializers and parsers, the YAML implementation uses a highly-efficient state machine for both serialization and parsing, converting directly between POJOs and YAML without intermediate DOM objects. New Classes​ YamlSerializer - Serializes POJOs to block-style YAML output. YamlParser - Parses YAML input into POJOs using an indentation-aware state machine. YamlWriter - Specialized writer for YAML output with key quoting and escape handling. Yaml - Convenience marshaller pairing YamlSerializer and YamlParser. @YamlConfig - Annotation for applying YAML configuration to REST resources. BasicYamlConfig - REST configuration interface for YAML-only resources. Features​ The YAML serializer produces clean, human-readable block-style output: Person person = new Person("John Smith", 30, List.of( new Address("100 Main St", "Anytown", "NY", 12345) )); String yaml = Yaml.of(person); Produces: name: John Smith age: 30 addresses: - street: 100 Main St city: Anytown state: NY zip: 12345 The parser supports the full range of YAML constructs including block/flow mappings and sequences, quoted and plain scalars, literal and folded block scalars, comments, document markers, and all standard YAML scalar types (null, booleans, numbers). Media Types​ Produces: application/yaml Accepts: application/yaml, text/yaml REST Integration​ YAML is included in BasicUniversalConfig by default, or can be used standalone via BasicYamlConfig. See YAML Basics for full documentation. YAML parser buffer-underflow fix on large documents (TODO-88)​ Fixed a latent java.io.IOException: Buffer underflow. thrown by YamlParser when round-tripping larger YAML documents whose deeply-indented lines crossed the parser's internal 1024-char read buffer. The shared org.apache.juneau.parser.ParserReader had a hard-coded 10-char unread lookback budget on the unmarked-refill path, but the YAML parser's indent handling (skipBlanksAndCountIndent + unreadSpaces(...), plus similar patterns in parseBlockScalar and isNullBlockValue) routinely needs to unread an entire line's leading indent at once — 12-20+ chars for deeply-nested OpenAPI 3.1 documents. When the indent read happened to cross the buffer boundary, only the last 10 of those chars survived the refill and the rest of the unreads underflowed. The fix widens that lookback budget from 10 to 256 chars (a new ParserReader.UNMARKED_LOOKBACK_CHARS constant). 256 covers any realistic YAML indent depth (128 levels at 2-space indent) while still leaving 768 chars per refill for forward-progress reads. The change has zero API surface — every parser benefits via the shared seam — and full utest suite (124k+ tests) runs at the same wall-clock as before. Acceptance test: the full BasicRestServlet OpenAPI 3.1 document (six api-docs URLs + full components.schemas set) now round-trips JSON → YAML → JSON cleanly. Previously OpenApiYamlRoundTrip_Test#c01 had to scope to a single OpenApiMixin mount via noInherit={"mixins"} to dodge the underflow; that workaround has been removed.

Iterator, Iterable (non-Collection), Enumeration, and java.util.stream.Stream types are now serialized directly as arrays by all serializers without requiring intermediate List materialization. Previously, Iterator and Enumeration objects were handled via IteratorSwap and EnumerationSwap which drained the entire sequence into a LinkedList before serialization began. Iterable (non-Collection) and Stream had no serialization support at all. Lazy serialization (no intermediate List): JSON, XML, UON, URL Encoding, and OpenAPI serializers write elements directly to the output one at a time via forEachStreamableEntry(). Materialized serialization (collected to List when the format requires it): MsgPack (protocol requires array size in header), HTML (inspects elements for table layout), and CSV (inspects first element for column headers) collect to a List internally. New API​ ClassMeta: New methods isIterator(), isIterable(), isStream(), isStreamable() for detecting these types. ClassMeta: New Category enum values ITERATOR, ITERABLE, STREAM. SerializerSession: New methods forEachStreamableEntry() and toListFromStreamable(). Example​ // Iterators are now serialized directly - no swap needed Iterator<String> iterator = List.of("foo", "bar", "baz").iterator(); String json = Json5Serializer.DEFAULT.serialize(iterator); // Produces: ['foo','bar','baz'] // Streams work the same way Stream<Integer> stream = Stream.of(1, 2, 3); String json2 = Json5Serializer.DEFAULT.serialize(stream); // Produces: [1,2,3] // Non-Collection Iterables are also supported Iterable<String> iterable = () -> List.of("a", "b").iterator(); String json3 = Json5Serializer.DEFAULT.serialize(iterable); // Produces: ['a','b'] Removals​ IteratorSwap - Removed. Iterators are now handled natively. EnumerationSwap - Removed. Enumerations are now handled natively. POJO Categories Update​ The POJO categories table has been updated. Iterator, Iterable, Enumeration, and Stream are no longer in the "swapped objects" category (group 4b). They are now in a new group (2c) alongside Collections and arrays as natively serializable sequence types.

New interfaces and annotations enable streaming serialization and parsing of arbitrarily large datasets without loading all elements into memory. Every serializer and parser format supports these APIs transparently. New Classes​ BeanSupplier<T> — Serialization-side streaming interface (extends Iterable<T>). Provides beans lazily from a cursor or query via begin(), iterator(), onError(), and complete() lifecycle methods. BeanConsumer<T> — Parse-side streaming interface (extends ThrowingConsumer<T>). Receives beans one-at-a-time from any parser for insertion or processing, with the same lifecycle methods. BeanChannel<T> — Combines BeanSupplier and BeanConsumer for round-trip marshalling on a single property. The same object drives both serialization and parsing. ListBeanChannel<T> — Built-in in-memory BeanChannel backed by an ArrayList, useful for testing and small in-memory datasets. BeanFactory<T> — Universal @FunctionalInterface for creating instances of any type, enabling integration with dependency-injection frameworks such as Spring. New Annotations​ @Bean(factory=X.class) — Specifies the BeanFactory class used to instantiate a type during parsing. The factory is resolved from the BeanStore (e.g. a Spring ApplicationContext). @Beanp(factory=X.class) — Property-level factory for a specific bean property value. @Beanp(elementType=Y.class) — Declares the element type for generic streaming properties (Stream<Y>, BeanSupplier<Y>, BeanConsumer<Y>, BeanChannel<Y>) to overcome Java type erasure. Also supports narrowing to concrete implementation types. New API​ BeanContext.Builder.beanStore(BeanStore) — Wires a BeanStore (e.g. SpringBeanStore) into the marshalling context so @Bean(factory=) factories can be resolved from a DI container. ParserSession.parseToBeanConsumer(Object, BeanConsumer<T>, Class<T>) — Parses an input source directly into a BeanConsumer, driving the full lifecycle automatically. Lifecycle​ All three interfaces share the same three-phase lifecycle: begin() for setup, the transfer method (iterator() or acceptThrows()) for element-by-element data flow, onError() for error handling, and complete() for cleanup. complete() is always called regardless of whether an error occurred. Key Behaviors​ Direction validation: using a BeanConsumer during serialization or a BeanSupplier during parsing throws an informative exception recommending BeanChannel for bidirectional use. Getter-only BeanConsumer properties: parsers reuse a BeanConsumer exposed via a getter (no setter required), calling acceptThrows() on the existing instance — matching the existing behavior for mutable Collection properties. Supplier<T> unwrapping: the standard JDK Supplier<T> (not BeanSupplier) is transparently unwrapped by serializers as a single lazy value, recursively up to depth 10. Stream<T> auto-close: java.util.stream.Stream objects used during serialization are automatically closed via try-with-resources after iteration completes. Example​ // Serialize a large table from a JDBC cursor — no memory materialization. @Bean(factory=EmployeeSupplier.Factory.class) public class EmployeeSupplier implements BeanSupplier<Employee> { private Connection conn; private ResultSet rs; @Override public void begin() throws Exception { conn = dataSource.getConnection(); rs = conn.prepareStatement("SELECT * FROM employee").executeQuery(); } @Override public Iterator<Employee> iterator() { return Employee.cursorIterator(rs); } @Override public void complete() throws Exception { rs.close(); conn.close(); } } // Bulk-insert with batch commits — no memory materialization. @Bean(factory=EmployeeConsumer.Factory.class) public class EmployeeConsumer implements BeanConsumer<Employee> { private Connection conn; private PreparedStatement stmt; private int count; @Override public void begin() throws Exception { conn = dataSource.getConnection(); conn.setAutoCommit(false); stmt = conn.prepareStatement("INSERT INTO employee (name, dept) VALUES (?,?)"); } @Override public void acceptThrows(Employee e) throws Exception { stmt.setString(1, e.getName()); stmt.setString(2, e.getDepartment()); stmt.executeUpdate(); if (++count % 500 == 0) conn.commit(); } @Override public void onError(Exception e) throws Exception { conn.rollback(); throw e; } @Override public void complete() throws Exception { conn.commit(); stmt.close(); conn.close(); } } See Large-Dataset Streaming for full documentation.

Java records are now fully supported for both serialization and parsing across all serializers and parsers. Records are treated as beans whose properties are derived from the record's components. The canonical constructor is automatically detected for parsing, so no @Beanc annotation is needed. public record Person(String name, int age) {} // Serialization String json = Json5Serializer.DEFAULT.serialize(new Person("John", 30)); // Produces: {age:30,name:'John'} // Parsing Person p = JsonParser.DEFAULT.parse("{\"name\":\"John\",\"age\":30}", Person.class); How It Works​ Property discovery: Record component accessor methods (e.g. name() for a name component) are recognized as getters without needing to follow the traditional getX() naming convention. Constructor detection: The canonical constructor is automatically identified. During parsing, property values are cached and then passed to the canonical constructor to create the record instance. Private fields: Record component fields are automatically included as bean properties despite being private final. Annotation Support​ The following annotations work with records: @Bean(properties) - Control property ordering (all components should be included). @Beanp(name) - Rename properties. @Beanc - Override the constructor used for parsing (e.g. to use a non-canonical constructor with defaults). @Bean(typeName) / @Bean(dictionary) - Polymorphic record types. Limitations​ Because records are immutable and all components must be provided to the canonical constructor, the following are not supported during parsing: @BeanIgnore on individual record components. @Bean(excludeProperties) excluding record components. @Bean(readOnlyProperties) / @Beanp(ro) on record components. These annotations will still affect serialization output. Use @Beanc with a non-canonical constructor to provide defaults for omitted components. Changes​ BeanMeta: Added record detection logic in constructor discovery, accessor method recognition, and field introspection. Records are exempt from beansRequireDefaultConstructor and beansRequireSomeProperties checks. BeanPropertyMeta: Constructor-arg properties are now correctly marked as writable. @BeanIgnore, @Bean, @Beanp, @Beanc: Javadocs updated with records-specific notes. See Java Records Support for full documentation.

Date, time, and duration types are now serialized and parsed natively as ISO 8601 strings by all serializers and parsers without requiring ObjectSwap registration. Previously, types such as Calendar, Date, Instant, ZonedDateTime, and other java.time.temporal.Temporal subtypes required default ObjectSwap instances (e.g. TemporalCalendarSwap, TemporalDateSwap) to be serialized as ISO 8601 strings. Without a swap, they would be serialized as beans or via toString(). Now, these types are recognized as first-class citizens by Juneau's type system and are handled directly in every serializer and parser session. Supported Types​ All java.time.temporal.Temporal subtypes: Instant, ZonedDateTime, OffsetDateTime, LocalDateTime, LocalDate, LocalTime, OffsetTime, Year, YearMonth Legacy date/time types: java.util.Calendar (and GregorianCalendar) java.util.Date javax.xml.datatype.XMLGregorianCalendar Duration type: java.time.Duration (serialized as ISO 8601 duration strings, e.g. "PT1H30M") How It Works​ Serialization: All serializers check ClassMeta.isDateOrCalendarOrTemporal() and ClassMeta.isDuration() before bean checks in their serializeAnything() dispatch. Matching objects are formatted via Iso8601Utils.format(). Parsing: All parsers check the same conditions in their parseAnything() dispatch. ISO 8601 strings are converted back to the target type via Iso8601Utils.parse(). Type conversions: BeanSession.convertToMemberType() and SerializerSession.toString() also use ISO 8601 formatting for these types, ensuring consistent behavior in map keys, bean properties, and other contexts. New API​ ClassMeta: New Category.DURATION enum value for java.time.Duration classification. ClassMeta: New method isDuration(). Iso8601Utils: New utility class centralizing ISO 8601 formatting and parsing for all date/time and duration types. Swap Classes as Overrides​ The existing swap classes (TemporalCalendarSwap, TemporalDateSwap, CalendarSwap, DateSwap, TemporalSwap) remain available but now serve as override mechanisms. If you register one of these swaps, it will take precedence over the built-in behavior, allowing you to customize the output format (e.g. RFC 1123 instead of ISO 8601). // Default behavior - no swap needed, uses ISO 8601 String json = JsonSerializer.DEFAULT.serialize(Calendar.getInstance()); // Produces: "2026-02-28T12:00:00Z" // Override with a swap for a different format JsonSerializer s = JsonSerializer.create() .swaps(TemporalCalendarSwap.Rfc1123DateTime.class) .build(); String json2 = s.serialize(Calendar.getInstance()); // Produces: "Sat, 28 Feb 2026 12:00:00 GMT" // Duration serialization - no swap needed String json3 = JsonSerializer.DEFAULT.serialize(Duration.ofHours(1).plusMinutes(30)); // Produces: "PT1H30M" POJO Categories Update​ The POJO categories table has been updated. Calendar, Date, Temporal subtypes, XMLGregorianCalendar, and Duration are no longer in the "swapped objects" category (group 4a). They are now in a new group (2d) as natively serializable date/time types. See POJO Categories for the updated table.

The juneau-marshall-rdf module now includes full support for RDF/THRIFT and RDF/PROTO binary serialization formats, enabling compact binary representation of RDF graphs for efficient storage and network transfer. New Classes​ RdfThriftSerializer - Serializes POJOs to RDF/THRIFT binary format. RdfThriftParser - Parses RDF/THRIFT binary input into POJOs. RdfThrift - Convenience marshaller pairing RdfThriftSerializer and RdfThriftParser. RdfProtoSerializer - Serializes POJOs to RDF/PROTO binary format. RdfProtoParser - Parses RDF/PROTO binary input into POJOs. RdfProto - Convenience marshaller pairing RdfProtoSerializer and RdfProtoParser. Features​ Both formats use Apache Jena for underlying RDF model handling, with compact binary encoding via Apache Thrift and Protocol Buffers respectively: Map<String,String> map = Map.of("foo", "bar"); // RDF/THRIFT byte[] thriftBytes = RdfThrift.of(map); Map<String,String> restored = RdfThrift.to(thriftBytes, Map.class, String.class, String.class); // RDF/PROTO byte[] protoBytes = RdfProto.of(map); Map<String,String> restored2 = RdfProto.to(protoBytes, Map.class, String.class, String.class); The binary formats are semantically equivalent to RDF/XML, RDF/JSON, and other RDF serializations—beans, maps, collections, and primitives are round-tripped correctly. Date/time types are parsed using built-in ISO 8601 support. Round-Trip Test Coverage​ RDF/XML, RDF/THRIFT, and RDF/PROTO are now included in the RoundTripTest_Base and ComboRoundTrip_Tester frameworks, validating round-trip correctness across a broad set of bean types, collections, and edge cases. See RDF Basics for full documentation.
documents.s: RDF/THRIFT and RDF/PROTO Binary Format Support

documents.t: ClassInfo.of(Class) now returns ClassInfoTyped<T>, a generic subclass of ClassInfo that preserves the type parameter at compile time. The API remains identical—existing code continues to work without changes—but callers can now benefit from stronger typing: ClassInfoTyped<String> ci = ClassInfo.of(String.class); // ci carries type information for String

Session.Builder.property(String, Object) and properties(Map) now dispatch to typed session-level setter methods across a broad range of serializer and parser session classes, enabling per-request override of serializer/parser configuration without rebuilding the context. Both short names (e.g. "escapeSolidus") and fully-qualified names (e.g. "JsonSerializerSession.escapeSolidus") are accepted as keys. BasicConverter handles type coercion so string values (e.g. "true") are automatically converted to the expected target types. // Per-request JSON settings without rebuilding the serializer String json = JsonSerializer.DEFAULT .createSession() .property("escapeSolidus", true) .property("addBeanTypes", true) .build() .serialize(myBean); // Per-request parser settings MyBean bean = JsonParser.DEFAULT .createSession() .property("trimStrings", true) .property("validateEnd", true) .build() .parse(json, MyBean.class); New Session-Level Properties​ Session Class New Property Keys ParserSession trimStrings JsonSerializerSession escapeSolidus JsonParserSession validateEnd UonSerializerSession encoding, paramFormat UonParserSession validateEnd UrlEncodingSerializerSession expandedParams UrlEncodingParserSession expandedParams XmlSerializerSession addNamespaceUrisToRoot, autoDetectNamespaces, defaultNamespace, enableNamespaces, textNodeDelimiter XmlParserSession preserveRootElement, validating HtmlSerializerSession addKeyValueTableHeaders, detectLabelParameters, detectLinksInStrings, labelParameter, uriAnchorText These complement the properties added in the initial release of this feature: BeanTraverseSession: initialDepth SerializerSession: keepNullProperties, trimStrings, addBeanTypes, addRootType, sortCollections, sortMaps, trimEmptyCollections, trimEmptyMaps WriterSerializerSession: maxIndent, quoteChar CsvSerializerSession: byteArrayFormat, allowNestedStructures, nullValue Bug Fixes — Context Bypass​ Several session classes were overriding accessor methods to return ctx.isAddBeanTypes() directly, bypassing the session-level field. This meant that per-session addBeanTypes overrides set via property("addBeanTypes", true) had no effect for those serializers. The affected classes now correctly delegate to super.isAddBeanTypes(): JsonSerializerSession, UonSerializerSession, XmlSerializerSession, HtmlSerializerSession, MsgPackSerializerSession, YamlSerializerSession, CborSerializerSession, BsonSerializerSession, RdfSerializerSession, RdfStreamSerializerSession Similarly, ParserSession.isTrimStrings() now returns the session-level field (initialized from the context) instead of delegating to ctx.isTrimStrings(). And UonSerializerSession.getQuoteChar() no longer bypasses the WriterSerializerSession session field.

A new utility class, org.apache.juneau.marshaller.MarshallUtils, provides a single point of static convenience methods for every serialization format supported by Juneau. All methods are designed to be used with a static import so call sites need no explicit marshaller reference. import static org.apache.juneau.marshaller.MarshallUtils.*; // Serialize to any text format — returns String String a = json(myBean); String b = json5(myBean); String c = xml(myBean); String d = html(myBean); String e = yaml(myBean); String f = csv(myBean); String g = toml(myBean); String h = hocon(myBean); // Serialize to binary formats — returns byte[] byte[] m = msgPack(myBean); byte[] n = cbor(myBean); byte[] o = bson(myBean); byte[] p = parquet(myBean); // Parse — same method names, overloaded by input type MyBean b1 = json(jsonString, MyBean.class); MyBean b2 = xml(xmlString, MyBean.class); MyBean b3 = msgPack(bytes, MyBean.class); List<MyBean> beans = parquet(bytes, MyBean.class); Supported Formats​ Method Format Output json(o) Standard JSON (RFC 8259) String json5(o) JSON5 String jsonl(o) JSON Lines (NDJSON) String jcs(o) Canonical JSON (RFC 8785) String hjson(o) HJSON String xml(o) XML String html(o) HTML String uon(o) URL-Encoded Object Notation String urlEncoding(o) URL Encoding String yaml(o) YAML String csv(o) CSV String openApi(o) OpenAPI String plainText(o) Plain text String markdown(o) Markdown (fragment) String markdownDoc(o) Markdown (document) String ini(o) INI / properties String toml(o) TOML String hocon(o) HOCON String proto(o) Protobuf Text Format String msgPack(o) MessagePack byte[] cbor(o) CBOR (RFC 8949) byte[] bson(o) BSON byte[] parquet(o) Apache Parquet byte[] Full Overload Set​ Every format method is overloaded across the following signatures: Signature Purpose format(Object) Serialize to String (text) or byte[] (binary) format(Object, Object) Serialize to a Writer, OutputStream, File, or StringBuilder format(Object, Class<T>) Parse from any input (String, byte[], File, Reader, etc.) — throws IOException format(Object, Type, Type...) Parse from any input with a parameterized type format(String, Class<T>) Parse from String — wraps exceptions in unchecked runtime exceptions format(String, Type, Type...) Parse from String with a parameterized type — unchecked format(byte[], Class<T>) Parse from byte[] (binary formats) — unchecked format(byte[], Type, Type...) Parse from byte[] with a parameterized type (binary formats) — unchecked The checked overloads (Object-based input) propagate ParseException and IOException. The String- and byte[]-based overloads wrap checked exceptions in unchecked runtime exceptions so they can be used directly in lambdas and streams without try/catch. All methods are designed for static import; no explicit marshaller reference is needed at call sites. Also updated: Jcs and Parquet marshallers​ Both marshaller classes were updated to expose the full static API: Jcs — Added of(Object, Object), to(Object, Class), to(Object, Type, Type...), to(String, Type, Type...) to match the standard char-marshaller contract. Parquet — Added of(Object, Object), to(Object, Class), to(Object, Type), to(byte[], Type, Type...) (Parquet parse methods return List<T> since the format is always collection-oriented).
documents.s: MarshallUtils: Static Serialization and Parsing Helpers

documents.t: The serialization helper methods on JsonMap and JsonList have been renamed from the asX() convention to the toX() convention and extended with additional JSON-flavor methods. Note: in the same release JsonMap.toString() / JsonList.toString() were retargeted from JSON5 to strict JSON as part of TODO-34 (see the "Neutral MarshalledMap / MarshalledList" section above). That means toJson() (not toJson5()) is now the synonym for toString(), and the rows below have been updated to reflect the new mapping. JsonMap​ New Method Description toJson() Serializes to strict RFC 8259 JSON (double-quoted keys/strings). Synonym for toString(). toJson5() Serializes to JSON5 — unquoted keys, single-quoted strings. toJsonl() Serializes to JSON Lines. toJcs() Serializes to Canonical JSON (RFC 8785). toHjson() Serializes to HJSON. toReadableJson5() Serializes to indented, human-readable JSON5. toString(WriterSerializer) Serializes using any WriterSerializer. JsonList​ New Method Description toJson() Serializes to strict RFC 8259 JSON. Synonym for toString(). toJson5() Serializes to JSON5. toJsonl() Serializes to JSON Lines. toJcs() Serializes to Canonical JSON (RFC 8785). toHjson() Serializes to HJSON. toString(WriterSerializer) Serializes using any WriterSerializer. Removed Methods​ The following asX() methods have been removed in favor of their toX() equivalents: Removed Replacement asJson() toJson() or toString() (now both strict JSON) asString() toString() — but note toString() is now strict JSON. Callers that genuinely want the old JSON5 form should switch to Json5Map.toString() / Json5List.toString() (or call toJson5() on JsonMap / JsonList). asReadableString() (JsonMap only) toReadableJson5() asString(WriterSerializer) toString(WriterSerializer)

documents.t: BasicBeanStore (in org.apache.juneau.cp) gained two new affordances that power the 9.5 RestContext precedence flip (see juneau-rest-server below). Both are opt-in; existing call sites that use only parent(...) and local addBean(...) calls keep their current behavior. Builder.overridingParent(BasicBeanStore) — Registers a parent bean store that is consulted before local entries during getBean(...) / getBeanSupplier(...). The classic parent(...) slot keeps its post-entry fallback role. Useful for bridging an outer scope (Spring ApplicationContext, parent-resource bootstrap, test harness) on top of a child bean store and having the outer scope win without mutating local entries. addDefaultSupplier(Class, Supplier) (and a named variant) — Registers a fallback supplier that fires only after local entries and the regular parent chain have all returned empty. Stored in a separate map from regular entries, so resolution order is unambiguous and addBean(...) calls can override the default at any time without removing the fallback. Final resolve order on BasicBeanStore is: overridingParent.getBeanSupplier(type, name) // outer scope (e.g. Spring) -> entries[type][name] // addBean(...) / @Bean -> parent.getBeanSupplier(type, name) // regular fallback -> defaults[type][name] // addDefaultSupplier(...) hasBean(...) follows the same precedence; a new hasDefaultSupplier(...) accessor lets callers ask "is there a registered default for this type?" without forcing the supplier to fire.

The following classes in org.apache.juneau.cp have been removed as part of the migration to the org.apache.juneau.commons.inject package: BasicBeanStore (was org.apache.juneau.cp.BasicBeanStore) — replaced by org.apache.juneau.commons.inject.BasicBeanStore (renamed from BasicBeanStore2). BeanCreator — replaced by org.apache.juneau.commons.inject.BeanInstantiator. BeanBuilder — replaced by org.apache.juneau.commons.inject.BeanInstantiator (was the base class for domain fluent builders; replaced with native builder fields and BeanInstantiator). BeanCreateMethodFinder — replaced by BeanStore.createBeanFromMethod(...). ContextBeanCreator is not removed — it solves a different problem (persistent Context.Builder holder for repeated annotation application) and is retained as a first-class API. Migration guide: Legacy (org.apache.juneau.cp) Replacement (org.apache.juneau.commons.inject) BasicBeanStore.create().build() new BasicBeanStore() BasicBeanStore.INSTANCE BasicBeanStore.INSTANCE BasicBeanStore.of(parent) new BasicBeanStore(parent) BeanCreator.of(MyBean.class, store) BeanInstantiator.of(MyBean.class, store) creator.arg(Type.class, value) instantiator.addBean(Type.class, value) creator.type(Impl.class) instantiator.type(Impl.class) creator.impl(instance) instantiator.impl(instance) creator.run() instantiator.run() creator.orElse(default) instantiator.asOptional().orElse(default) new BeanCreateMethodFinder(type, obj, bs) bs.createBeanFromMethod(type, obj, predicate)
